name: fcrackzip - ZIP Archive Password Cracking
description: fcrackzip cracks password-protected ZIP archives via dictionary or brute-force attack directly (no hash extraction needed). Fast for quick ZIP cracks in CTF and loot scenarios. For stronger/other formats, extract a hash with zip2john and crack with hashcat/john instead.
notes:
=== DICTIONARY ATTACK ===
  fcrackzip -u -D -p <wordlist> secret.zip
  #  -u  unzip to verify (removes false positives)
  #  -D  dictionary mode
  #  -p  wordlist file
  fcrackzip -u -D -p /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt secret.zip

=== BRUTE FORCE ===
  fcrackzip -u -b -c a1 -l 1-6 secret.zip
  #  -b        brute force
  #  -c a1     charset: lowercase + digits
  #  -l 1-6    length range
  #  -c aA1!   add upper + symbols

=== VERBOSE / SHOW PROGRESS ===
  fcrackzip -v -u -D -p rockyou.txt secret.zip

=== PREFERRED FOR MODERN/AES ZIPS -> use john/hashcat ===
  zip2john secret.zip > zip.hash
  john --wordlist=rockyou.txt zip.hash
  # or: hashcat -m 13600 zip.hash rockyou.txt   (WinZip AES)
  # or: hashcat -m 17210/17220/17225 for PKZIP variants

=== OTHER ARCHIVE FORMATS ===
  rar2john file.rar | hashcat -m 13000
  7z2john file.7z   | hashcat -m 11600

examples.label: Hash route for AES ZIP
examples.command: zip2john secret.zip > zip.hash && hashcat -m 13600 zip.hash rockyou.txt

recommended.note: Extract a ZIP hash to crack with john/hashcat (handles AES ZIPs).
Crack the extracted archive hash with hashcat.
Hidden data is often in images, not just archives.

defense.why_it_works: ZIP encryption (especially legacy ZipCrypto) is weak and offline-crackable. Weak passwords fall quickly to dictionary/brute force since the attacker controls the file.
defense.prerequisites: Possession of the encrypted archive; a wordlist or compute for brute force.
defense.impact: Recovery of archive contents (often credentials, keys, documents).
defense.detection: Offline attacker-side activity - not detectable on the target.
defense.artifacts: fcrackzip/zip2john on the attacker host only.
defense.prevention: Use strong, long passphrases; use AES-256 ZIP or GPG/7z-AES instead of legacy ZipCrypto; do not ship secrets in weakly encrypted archives.
